clue.text: After a little time, Lincoln backed one of very little order

indicators.note: the reversed name is placed after the bit of time, so it comes second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short spell of time

indicators.note: backed means the name is read from end to start

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US president Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A tale of President Lincoln's views on some small matter of procedure after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ABE into EBA. 'order' is the biological rank, and a single-celled creature belongs to a very lowly one.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled organism is about as tiny and simple a living thing as biology classifies, so it belongs to a very little order.

clue.text: Topless mayhem at a party (one's heavily stoned)

indicators.note: topless says the word loses its first letter, its top in a down entry

parts.note: havoc is mayhem, chaos
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Wild scenes at a party where people strip off, with one guest very high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' takes the H off HAVOC to leave AVOC. 'stoned' sounds like drug-taking but means having a stone: the fruit has a large one.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit in question has a single very large stone at its centre, hence heavily stoned.

clue.text: Vicious dictator with gun raised in agony after two rounds by 18 4

indicators.note: the agony with its contents follows the two rounds

parts.note: two rounds are two O shapes, rings

indicators.note: in places the dictator group within the word for agony

parts.note: pain is agony
Sid Vicious was the bassist of the punk band the Sex Pistols
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A cruel tyrant, weapon held aloft, suffering after a couple of boxing rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Sid Vicious played bass for the punk band the Sex Pistols, so the surname stands for the first name. 'raised' reverses the gun in this down entry; the agony word is split around the rest. 18 4 is BRITNEY SPEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 2000 hit single recorded by the pop singer named by 18 4.

clue.text: Jew's heading off to Rome, returning after ancient kingdom has licentious leader ousted by 18 4

indicators.note: the reversed run comes after the shortened kingdom
ousted says that letter is pushed out of the kingdom's name

parts.note: Babylon was an ancient Mesopotamian kingdom, famed for licentiousness

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
returning means the run is read backwards
heading off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a Jew is a Semite
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Jewish traveller decapitated en route to Rome, after an ancient decadent kingdom loses its ringleader.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing L from BABYLON gives BABYON; EMITE (SEMITE headless) plus ROME, read backwards by 'returning', gives EMORETIME. The answer is Britney Spears's debut single.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the 1998 debut single recorded by the pop singer named by 18 4.

clue.text: See 18
Don't allow for insect being upright

indicators.note: don't tells us to drop the phrase that follows from the insect

parts.note: a caterpillar is an insect larva
to cater for something is to allow for it

explanation.surface: An instruction not to make room for a bug standing on its hind legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't allow for' reads as 'don't cater for', so CATER comes off the larva's name. 'upright' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical structural support, the same thing as a column.

clue.text: A danger to ignore English pudding, one taken in seasonally

indicators.note: to ignore means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: peril is danger
a fool is a British pudding of fruit puree folded into cream

explanation.surface: Warning of the risk of skipping English desserts, with one diner duped once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' drops E from PERIL to leave PRIL. A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricked on the first of April by a prank is taken in at that time of year.

clue.text: Provide honey, perhaps, with kiss ultimately (little X)

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Instructions to give your darling an affectionate word and a small kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honey' sounds like a sweetheart but is the sweet substance; adding it makes food sweeter. X is also a kiss, adding to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding honey to food or drink is one way to make it taste sweeter.

clue.text: Compiles a true cryptic that in prospect is sought …

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the preceding letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A setter boasting of putting together a genuine cryptic puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in prospect' means while prospecting: gold or silver is what a prospector looks for. The clue runs on into 14 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospectors search the ground for gold, silver and similar valuable ores.

clue.text: Englishman abroad afforded quiet ceremony

parts.note: Pom is Australian and New Zealand slang for an English person
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A British expatriate was allowed a low-key ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is stately display and splendour, as at a ceremony.

clue.text: Worm turned by serial criminal's crimes

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a grub is a worm-like larva

indicators.note: criminal here signals the letters are rearranged illegally

explanation.surface: A worm turning the tables on a serial offender's misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes BURG of GRUB; 'criminal's' makes LARIES of SERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Break-ins to steal from buildings are a class of crimes.

clue.text: Establishment raking it in, so accountant's in love

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant, plus 's for is
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A business making money hand over fist, so its bookkeeper is smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is a chartered accountant, and the 's stays as S. 'raking it in' describes the house winning.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house rakes in the stakes, literally with a croupier's rake.

clue.text: Strings of beads embellishing the scalp

indicators.note: embellishing suggests dressing up the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beaded necklaces worn as ornaments on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a string of beads, a short rosary or a garland worn on the head.

clue.text: See 15
… by St Michael, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing 8 down: gold sought by a saint, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Read on from 8 down: precious metal is what an alchemist sought, by turning base metal into gold. 'St Michael' is also the old Marks & Spencer brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners of this pseudo-science sought to transmute base metal into gold.

clue.text: A prophet, my boy, on a UK tour by 18 4

indicators.note: a tour moves around, so the letters go round into a new order

parts.words: A prophet, my boy, on a UK

explanation.surface: A father tells his son a prophet is touring Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 4 is BRITNEY SPEARS; this is one of her hits.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1999 single recorded by the pop singer named by 18 4.

clue.text: Tilt jauntily at mate

definitions.meaning: to tilt a hat at a rakish angle
a British, especially Cockney, form of address for a friend

explanation.definitionFit: One word means to set a hat at a jaunty angle and is also old London slang for a pal.

clue.text: Bill's affectionate partner left before his cavorting, which is quite refreshing

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the rearranged word

parts.note: to bill and coo is to kiss and murmur, so coo partners bill

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Bill's sweetheart walks out ahead of his capering, which is a welcome relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is from 'bill and coo'. 'cavorting' turns HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat cold, as a light breeze is, can be described as quite refreshing.

clue.text: Working out ably, I suit fitness

indicators.note: working out means solving or reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gym-goer exercising competently claims that training suits their fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: Usability is how fit something is for use, its suitability.

clue.text: Phenomenal moralist Presbyterians proved to be false

indicators.note: proved to be false means the word is not what it seems, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Puritan churchgoers turned out to be hypocrites.
explanation.walkthrough: The pop star once publicly championed virginity before marriage, hence the ironic 'moralist'; 'phenomenal' points to her pop stardom.
explanation.definitionFit: The pop phenomenon who long professed abstinence before marriage is wryly called a moralist.

clue.text: Part-timers to invest pound in financial centre, as it's understood

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was the UK's reserve force of part-time soldiers

indicators.note: in places the money inside the financial district

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: Weekend soldiers putting their money into the City.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) was Britain's volunteer reserve; 'the City' is the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done tacitly is understood or implied without being spoken.

clue.text: 18 4's much vaunted sign conceals a vixen!

indicators.note: conceals means the sign holds a letter inside it

parts.note: Virgo, the virgin, the star sign that sums up the singer's much-publicised virginity

explanation.surface: The pop star's boasted star sign hides a shrew inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 4 is BRITNEY SPEARS, known for proclaiming her virginity, hence VIRGO, the virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: A vixen in this sense is a shrewish, quarrelsome woman, the same as a virago.

clue.text: See 3
Where Odysseus lived with a cat without wings

indicators.note: without wings means dropping the outer letters of the phrase, leaving the run inside it

explanation.surface: The Greek hero's home, shared with a cat that cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus was king of this Greek island, to which he spent ten years returning.

clue.text: See 15
See 2
Plant tissue in marrow

definitions.meaning: spongy tissue in the stems of plants
the essential core of something, or spinal marrow

explanation.definitionFit: The word names spongy stem tissue and also the soft inner core or marrow of something.

clue.text: Fast car when stolen drove endlessly

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rode is a synonym of drove, travelled

explanation.surface: The fast car was stolen and driven without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A souped-up car modified for speed is known by this American slang term.

clue.text: Origins of Selene, Zeus and Gaia all take years to achieve celestial alignment

annotationWithheld.why: Origins of Selene, Zeus and Gaia all take years to achieve celestial alignment: S, Z and G each take a Y (SY+ZY+GY); 'Origins of' must serve three picks and 'years' give three Ys, which the grammar refuses as a shared indicator and repeated leaf
annotationWithheld.clue: Origins of Selene, Zeus and Gaia all take years to achieve celestial alignment
